title: Preface
summary: A 1972 HEXAGON memo describes the deep-sea recovery of recovery vehicle 1201-3, lost July 1971 at about 16,000 ft after a parachute failure. USNS De Steiger located it in October 1971, and Trieste II made three attempts; the third recovered only 25 feet of film, which broke during surfacing. Analysis shows the vehicle broke up on impact with little corrosion. Lessons cover integrated search, weather dependence, Trieste II reliability failures, and IOU mobility limits. The mission's success was the demonstrated deep-sea recovery capability.

title: ATTACHMENTl - to BYE-108849-72
summary: Attachment to a 9 February 1972 memo, trip report on RV-3 recovery. The in-air recovery failed on 10 July when a parachute failed; the RV hit the open sea at about 2600 g and 310 mph, and its impact area was calculated. Because the intelligence was valuable, the Navy was asked to provide deep-submergence search and recovery at an estimated 14,000 ft depth, using the USNS DeSteiger and the Trieste II submersible, funded by NRO. Recovery equipment was built and a dummy RV recovery practice off San Diego failed due to Trieste equipment problems.

title: I U SECRET HEXAGON

nodes.title: I U SECRET HEXAGON (intro)
nodes.summary: Trip report on RV-3 recovery operations by the Trieste. Covers three criteria: environment (keeping the recovered RV at ~40°F and ocean-like humidity; Navy's insulated box and dry ice fell short at 55°F and 48°F, so a leased walk-in refrigerator was used), light (black shroud placed at 80-100 ft and night surfacing to protect film), and security (five officers briefed, cover story of an MPL instrumentation package, and inadvertent disclosure forms for divers).

nodes.title: -fOP-5ERET-HEXAGON
nodes.summary: Trip report on RV-3 recovery operations: the DeSteiger found the RV on 8 October using Deep Ocean Transponders and a pinger, with underwater photos suggesting the TU remained intact. The Integrated Operating Unit (White Sands with Trieste) sailed 11 October, arrived 1 November, and gassed and shotted Trieste. The 5 November dive located DOT positions but could not visually confirm targets, owing to a failed trail ball, sonar offset, and silt. Rough seas forced return to Pearl Harbor on 16 November, and COMSUBPAC approved further attempts with added support.

nodes.title: -TOP-5tCRET HEXAGON
-TOP-5tCRET HEXAGON (intro)
nodes.summary: Trip report on RV-3 recovery operations by the submersible Trieste. The task element left Pearl Harbor 21 Nov; a grounded battery cell proved to be minor wiring error; sea conditions delayed launch until 29 Nov. On the 30 Nov dive, a shot releaser leak caused a list, and control was lost until about 7000 ft. Near the bottom, DOTs were located about 5000 ft away, requiring a two-hour transit. Equipment failures included computer power loss, trail ball problems, and a port skeg dragging the bottom. Trieste sighted the payload, but low battery prevented placing a DOT, and it surfaced 1 Dec. Storm towing to port for repairs followed. The IOU returned to Pearl Harbor in February and plans to return about 15 March.

nodes.title: C. FUTURE PLANS
C. FUTURE PLANS (intro)
nodes.summary: Describes Navy plans to recover RV-3: IOU stays at Pearl Harbor, returns to the operating site about 15 March, and White Sands dry-docked for repair of two of three station keepers. Trieste to be launched for another dive once seas permit; writer travels to Pearl Harbor when launch is committed, reaching IOU by helicopter, about 60 hours needed to prepare Trieste. Writer is ready to brief on operations to date or after recovery attempts. Includes distribution list and a 24 May 1972 memorandum header for Trip Report, Recovery of 1201-3.

nodes.title: Introduction
nodes.summary: A trip report for 16-26 April covering recovery of film stacks from RV-3. On Sunday 16 April, the author arrived in Honolulu, was met by Lt. Bazzel (USN) and Lt. Col. Tweedy (USAF), and went to Pearl Harbor. Concern arose about keeping the film cool; dry ice was planned for the shipping container. USS Safeguard left at 1730 as standby tug while Trieste was in the water ready to dive.

nodes.title: Monday, 17 April
nodes.summary: Naval log entries, 17-19 April: the Apache/White Sands/Trieste was met late on 17 April, but rough seas (12-15 ft) halted small-boat transfers and dive operations. On 18 April the Safeguard, a fleet salvage ship with booms, divers and a machine shop, was ordered to Kauai to transfer personnel to a relief ship, then return to Pearl Harbor. On 19 April the USS Bolster, same class, met the Safeguard and transferred personnel at Kauai.

nodes.title: Thursday, 20 April
nodes.summary: Trip report of a 1201-3 recovery mission, 20-25 April. Covers rendezvous with the IOU, radio silence due to a Russian ship, a sailor transferred by small boat and helicopter, and deteriorating weather (8-12 ft seas). Trieste checkout and shotting on 24 April: ground fault isolated to amp-hour meter and replaced; 25 April: wave soaked electronics, shorts in computer power supply and inverter, DOT transponder recovery by hydroplane. Dive began 25 April at 1800; sonar contacts in a debris field, RV sighted, and hook engaged on sixth attempt before surfacing.

nodes.title: 26 April
nodes.summary: Trieste II surfaced to report the payload had disintegrated in silt, with pieces lost through the hook; divers recovered some film. Pilots were debriefed at White Sands; corrosion was blamed. Trip report notes transfer to the Bolster for return to Pearl Harbor. Attachment IV analyzes the recovered takeup: photos show canister gold foil, film spools, encoder, motor electronics, and a shattered beryllium core. Kodak found 25 feet of film torn into five pieces, likely cut by spokes on impact. The upper RV structure remains on the ocean bottom.

Trip report covering the 16-26 April recovery of RV-3 film stacks: Honolulu arrival, Pearl Harbor logistics, rough seas delaying operations, Safeguard and Bolster personnel transfers at Kauai, Trieste checkout and dive, and the RV hook-up on the sixth attempt. The payload disintegrated in silt, film was partly recovered, and the upper RV structure remains on the bottom. Future plans: IOU stays at Pearl Harbor, White Sands dry-docked for repairs, and Trieste relaunched for another dive once seas permit, with the writer ready to brief on operations.

Trip report on RV-3 recovery by submersible Trieste: a grounded battery cell was a wiring error, launch was delayed by sea conditions, and a shot releaser leak caused a list and loss of control until about 7000 ft. DOTs were located about 5000 ft away after a two-hour transit, and equipment failures (computer power, trail ball, port skeg) hampered operations. Trieste sighted the payload but could not place a DOT due to low battery, then surfaced and was towed to port. The IOU returned to Pearl Harbor in February. A second report covers the 16-26 April recovery of RV-3 film stacks: rough seas, personnel transfers at Kauai, a sixth-attempt RV hook-up, partial film recovery as the payload disintegrated in silt, and the upper RV structure left on the bottom. Future plans: IOU stays at Pearl Harbor, White Sands dry-docked for repairs, and Trieste relaunched once seas permit.

summary: Trip reports on RV-3 recovery by the submersible Trieste. Covers environment (keeping the RV cool and humid; a leased walk-in refrigerator was needed), light (black shroud, night surfacing), and security (briefed officers, MPL cover story, disclosure forms). Also covers DeSteiger's October location of the RV, the November dive that failed to visually confirm targets, a grounded battery wiring error, a shot releaser leak, equipment failures, and the April film-stack recovery, where partial film was recovered and the upper RV structure was left on the bottom. Future plans: dry-dock repairs and relaunch when seas permit.

title: HEXAGON SECRET
summary: Declassified HEXAGON-program report (BYE-108849-72, Attachment IV) analyzing Trieste II underwater photographs of recovered debris from a film-return canister: gold canister foil, support arms, film spools, encoder and motor electronics, and a shattered beryllium takeup core. Kodak found the 25 feet of recovered film physically unchanged but torn into five pieces, likely from spokes cutting the film on impact. Film flaked off during surfacing. The upper RV structure remains on the ocean bottom. Figures IV A-J are referenced.
